headline: SOFTER AUGUST PCE: CORE INFLATION AT 3.0% — GOLD JUMPS 0.7% TO $4,210 AS OCTOBER RATE HIKE ODDS FALL TO 37%
snippet: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge came in well below expectations on September 30 — August core PCE rose just 0.2% month-on-month and 3.0% year-on-year, versus consensus of 0.3% and 3.3% respectively. Gold responded by jumping 0.73% to $4,210/oz while traders cut October rate hike odds from ~45% to 37%; elevated Treasury yields and a strong dollar kept gains contained, and gold still finished September down roughly 5.4% — its worst monthly performance since early 2025.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS COWBOY STATE: US$1.07B NPV, 4.5 MTPA, 26-YEAR MINE PLAN — U.S. NdPr OUTPUT TARGETS 2,500 T/YR
snippet: American Rare Earths Limited (ASX: ARR) released an updated scoping study September 30 for the Cowboy State Mine at Halleck Creek, Wyoming — after-tax NPV of US$1.07 billion at 8% real discount rate, throughput scaled 50% to 4.5 million tonnes per annum, average annual NdPr oxide production of 2,500 tonnes (+36% on 2025 base case), and a mine life extended to 26 years. Initial capex is estimated at ~US$900 million inclusive of contingency. A pre-feasibility study is the next milestone for what would be one of the largest domestic U.S. rare earth operations, at a moment when the White House is actively funding critical-mineral alternatives to Chinese supply.

headline: GOLD FIELDS WEIGHS SWEETENED BID FOR NORTHERN STAR — EXPLORING HIGHER CASH AFTER A$38.7B REBUFF
snippet: Gold Fields Ltd. (NYSE: GFI) is reviewing an enhanced offer for Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST), exploring a higher cash component after NST's board rejected the initial A$38.7 billion proposal on September 24 as "opportunistic," Bloomberg reported September 29. GFI ADRs rose 4.8% and NST gained 1.8% on the news. A sweetened deal at a premium above the original 22% would still target the second-largest global gold producer at ~4.1 Moz annual output with up to US$5 billion in estimated synergies — the largest active M&A bid in the gold sector.

headline: NEWMONT: $5.3B FREE CASH FLOW IN JUST SIX MONTHS, $6B BUYBACK LAUNCHED — 9% OF SHARES CANCELLED AT RECORD GOLD PRICES
snippet: Newmont Corp. (NYSE: NEM) presented at Mining Forum Americas 2026 on September 29 reporting a record $5.3 billion in free cash flow through the first six months of 2026, and a new $6 billion share repurchase authorization after completing prior programs. The company has cancelled more than 100 million shares — reducing the count by approximately 9% — and management signalled the capital-return formula supports an 8% quarterly dividend increase at the next annual review. At $4,000+ gold, Newmont's earnings mechanics are converting record commodity prices directly into per-share value growth.

headline: ESCONDIDA STRIKE VOTE CLOSES TODAY — COPPER HOLDS ABOVE $14,400/T AS WORLD'S LARGEST MINE TEETERS
snippet: Chile's Escondida No. 2 supervisors' union concluded its strike vote September 30 at the world's largest copper mine (BHP, ~5% of global supply) after unanimously rejecting BHP's latest wage offer and urging members to vote no. LME copper held above $14,400/tonne — a third consecutive monthly gain — on the strike risk premium, weeks after Comex copper set an all-time record of $6.83/lb on September 22. A strike vote majority triggers mandatory five-day government mediation before workers can legally walk out, keeping supply disruption risk elevated into Q4.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS ANTINO: 27m @ 20.38 G/T GOLD IN FIRST STEP-OUT ON NEW WEST ZONE — SURINAME DISTRICT NOW 6 TARGETS
snippet: Founders Metals Corp. (TSX-V: FDR) reported September 29 at Mining Forum Americas 2026 that its first step-out hole on the newly identified West Zone at the Antino Gold Project in Suriname returned 27.0 metres at 20.38 g/t gold, one of three high-grade hits across the district in the current drill program alongside 28m at 14 g/t and 15.5m at 30 g/t. Six distinct targets are now active across the land package, with a fall drill program planned for Antino North — at high-grade intervals like these in a low-cost jurisdiction, Antino is one of the most active exploration-stage gold stories in South America.

headline: EMPEROR METALS DUQUESNE WEST: 32m @ 5.9 G/T GOLD INCLUDING 2.6m @ 22.4 G/T AT 335m DEPTH — ZONE THICKENING
snippet: Emperor Metals Inc. reported September 29 the completion of its 2026 campaign at Duquesne West in Abitibi, Quebec — 66 holes totalling 20,479 metres — with highlight hole DQ26-37 returning 32.0 metres at 5.9 g/t gold from 335 metres depth including 2.6 metres at 22.4 g/t, confirming local thickening of the replacement-style mineralization system. Assays are in on 44 of 66 holes with the remainder pending; for investors tracking Abitibi gold explorers, consistent high-grade results at depth across a completed drill campaign set up a compelling NI 43-101 resource estimate.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY CORP: 157% Q4 PRODUCTION SURGE TO 82,744 LBS — $93.13/LB REALIZED PRICE, $753M WAR CHEST AT YEAR-END
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) released fiscal year 2026 results September 30 headlined by a 157% Q4 production surge to 82,744 pounds of U3O8 — its strongest quarterly output — at a combined cost of $36.54/lb after scale economies at Christensen Ranch (Wyoming) and the first full quarter of Burke Hollow (Texas) ISR operations. A $93.13/lb unhedged realized sales price on 400,000 lbs sold from inventory delivered $37.3 million in revenue and $16.9 million gross profit; the company enters fiscal 2027 with a combined cash and inventory war chest of approximately $753 million at a spot uranium price near $89.50/lb.

headline: DUNDEE PRECIOUS METALS BALKANS: 50m @ 3.68% CuEq DISCOVERED 1KM UNDERGROUND — 300m BEYOND CURRENT RESOURCE EDGE
snippet: Dundee Precious Metals Inc. (TSX: DPM) highlighted a new underground copper-gold-silver discovery in the Balkans at Mining Forum Americas 2026 on September 29 — 50 metres at 3.68% copper equivalent encountered approximately 1 kilometre underground and 300 metres beyond the current extent of its existing operations. Management described it as a major potential growth driver for an already-cash-generative producing company; follow-up drilling is planned. For investors tracking copper-gold systems in proven European mining districts, a 3.68% CuEq intercept at depth is a legitimate resource extension catalyst.

headline: Q3 IN THE BOOKS: $4,400 GOLD AVERAGE, RECORD CASH FLOWS — RUBINO ON WHY MINERS' BEST QUARTERS ARE STILL AHEAD
snippet: Analyst John Rubino published a September 27 Q3 wrap-up noting gold and silver averaged $4,400/oz and $64/oz in Q3 respectively — just marginally below Q2's $4,500 and $71 — with higher oil costs from Iran-related supply disruptions shaving a few margin points but the best-run miners still on track for record-or-near-record cash flows. Earnings season opens October 22 with Newmont's results. Rubino's key point: miners have spent the past year paying down debt and building cash balances, so interest expense is falling even as energy costs rise, compounding the earnings power of $4,000+ gold into a structural bull case for junior mining equities.
